sq.q: A Prolog program must find all ways to solve a puzzle. How is backtracking useful here?
answer: Backtracking lets Prolog explore all possible rule matches by reverting to earlier states. It automatically tries different combinations to find valid solutions. This makes Prolog ideal for solving search and constraint problems.

sq.q: How do control structures in logic programming differ from procedural languages?
answer: Logic programming uses rules and logical inference instead of sequential control flow. There's no explicit loop or if ; control is driven by matching facts and goals. This leads to a more declarative and concise representation.

2. Prolog Program Using Structures and Demonstrating Backtracking (6 marks)

% Facts: disease(Name, [List of symptoms]) disease(flu, [fever, cough, fatigue]). disease(covid, [fever, cough, loss_of_smell]). disease(malaria, [fever, chills, sweating]). disease(cold, [cough, sneezing, sore_throat]).
% Rule to check if a disease has all given symptoms has_symptoms(Disease, Symptoms) :- disease(Disease, SymptomList), subset(Symptoms, SymptomList).

% Helper rule to check if all elements of one list are in another subset([], _). subset([H|T], List) :- member(H, List), subset(T, List). Sample Query ?- has_symptoms(D, [fever, cough]). D = flu ; D = covid ; false.
